claims.text: A full charge-density scheme with a kinetic-energy correction is a method for evaluating ground-state properties.
A full charge-density scheme with a kinetic-energy correction can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy alloys.
The determination is applicable under variable temperatures and magnetic fields.
Configurational entropy acts as a structural mediator of the magnetic behavior.
The average ionic radius of the A-site cation acts as a structural mediator in the high-entropy alloys.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties is attributable to configurational entropy and the average A-site ionic radius.
Configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius influence the intensity of indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius influence the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
